chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty: 'And when the buried female infant is asked, for what sin was she killed?' He said: 'It was revealed about Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali, the third Imam
key_terms.الْمَوْؤُدَةُ: The buried female infant, specifically one buried alive in pre-Islamic Arabia, here interpreted as Al-Husayn (a.s.)
key_terms.بِسَبَبِ أَيِّ ذَنْبٍ: For what sin (questioned on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.نَزَلَتْ: It was revealed (referring to the occasion of revelation)

ai.seo_question: Who is the buried female infant (Al-Maw'udah) in Surah Al-Takwir referring to according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* offers a distinctive Shia exegetical view, identifying Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) as the specific referent for the 'buried female infant' (Al-Maw'udah) in Surah At-Takwir, thereby elevating his martyrdom to the status of a Quranic archetype. By linking the verse's question 'For what sin was she killed?' to Al-Husayn, the hadith emphasizes the innocence of the Ahl al-Bayt and frames their suffering as a central theme of divine justice. This interpretation underscores the theological significance of the Battle of Karbala as a pivotal event foretold and validated by the Quran itself.
